_description: Soil domain: ICAR classification of Indian soils (8 major types), soil categories, and soil science concepts. Every entity links to locations via found_in.

attributes.area_share: Largest soil group, ~40% of India's land area

attributes.fertility: Very low organic matter, high salinity in places
Rich in lime, iron, magnesium, alumina; poor in nitrogen and phosphorus
attributes.special: Self-ploughing (cracks in summer), swells when wet

attributes.note: Problem soils require reclamation before cultivation
attributes.type: Acidic, saline, alkaline/sodic, waterlogged, saline-alkali, peaty/marshy, eroded, sandy

attributes.character: Layered with forest litter; acidic in high-rainfall hills
attributes.fertility: Rich in humus in forested areas; shallow in steep slopes
attributes.origin: Weathering in situ in hills and mountains

attributes.colour: Reddish-brown to yellow (iron and aluminium oxides)
attributes.fertility: Low humus; acidic; responds to fertilizers and irrigation

attributes.coverage: Classified on basis of formation, colour, texture, chemistry

attributes.fertility: High organic carbon; requires drainage for crops
attributes.origin: Waterlogged, low-lying areas with organic accumulation

attributes.note: Low pH; liming recommended; NE India, Kerala, WB
High soluble salts; coastal (WB Sundarbans, TN coast, Kerala backwaters, MH Konkan) and arid areas; reclamation via leaching + drainage
High exchangeable sodium; reclamation with gypsum; UP usar land
Excess moisture, poor aeration; canal command areas

attributes.fertility: Poor in nitrogen, phosphorus, humus; responds to manuring

attributes.character: High soluble salts (saline) or high sodium (alkaline/sodic)
attributes.fertility: Low productivity; reclaimable (gypsum for alkali, leaching for saline)
attributes.origin: Poor drainage, high evapotranspiration, canal seepage

attributes.use: Soil nutrient status (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B) and fertiliser recommendation

attributes.note: Topsoil and nutrient loss by water/wind erosion; ICAR problem soil. Widespread, concentrated in the Shiwalik foothills and hilly tracts of HP/Uttarakhand and parts of the Deccan plateau.

Coarse-textured, low water-holding capacity, high infiltration and leaching losses; a problem soil needing organic matter and mulching. Dominant in western Rajasthan and the Kachchh region of Gujarat.
